title: 为什么沉浸式模拟游戏仍然值得做——对话 Harvey Smith 与 Ben Horne

Why it's still worth making immersive sims
Design
Business
Interviews
The official podcast for GameDeveloper.com brings you illuminating conversation and commentary from brilliant people in the video game industry.
Why it's still worth making immersive sims ft. Harvey Smith & Ben Horne
Celebrated game designer Harvey Smith and former Arkane Austin executive producer Ben Horne lay out their vision for Black Pony Immersive.
Game Developer Podcast
October 5, 2026
What happens when you're a talented game designer who's helped make proven hits in a genre that financial analysts are bemoaning as niche? Do you go make what's popular? Or do you fight like hell to make the games of your dreams?
These are the kind of questions you might ask former Arkane Studios collaborators and
Black Pony Immersive
co-founders Harvey Smith and Ben Horne, who are dead-set on making the kinds of ambitious games that defined the celebrated studio behind
Dishonored
,
Prey
, and
Deathloop
: first-person action-RPG 'immersive sims' with style and character.
They'd be the first to tell you it takes creativity and gumption to make these kinds of games when you don't have the backing of multi-million dollar companies like Zenimax or Microsoft behind you. So what are the 'first principles' of immersive sims, and how are Smith and Horne thinking about building these kinds of games at an all-new studio?
Related:
The art of game writing in 'non-narrative' games ft. Emma Kidwell and Harrison Pink
You'll find the answers on this week's episode of the Game Developer Podcast.
About the Game Developer Podcast
The Game Developer podcast is a bi-weekly podcast chronicling the triumphs, catastrophes, and everything in-between of game development, sharing lessons and strategies fellow developers can use to hone their craft. The Game Developer Podcast is hosted by Bryant Francis, edited by Pierre Landriau, and features music by
Mike Meehan
.
